cause: Math.floor truncates the final discounted cents instead of rounding half upward.
action: Use Math.round once on the final discounted total, preserving the pre-discount safe-integer checks. Added half-cent, neighboring percent and multi-night regressions.

cause: Inclusive endpoint comparisons treat adjoining half-open stays as overlapping.
action: Use strict endpoint comparisons. Added adjacency regressions in both argument orders and overlapping controls.

cause: The encoder omits single quotes, leaving the single-quoted attribute delimiter unescaped.
action: Encode all five special characters with one replacement pass. Added exact-output regressions for apostrophes, all special characters and pre-existing entity text.

cause: confirmed <= capacity admits enrollment when a class is already full, including zero capacity.
action: Require confirmed < capacity. Added full, zero-capacity, over-capacity and available-capacity regressions.

cause: A strict greater-than comparison excludes cancellation exactly 24 hours before the start.
action: Include the 86400000-millisecond boundary with >=. Added exact-boundary, adjacent-millisecond, equal-start and after-start cases.

cause: Array.sort runs directly on the supplied array, mutating its order and returning the same array.
action: Sort a shallow array copy. Added stable-tie, input-order, record-sharing, frozen-input and empty/singleton new-array regressions.

cause: The accumulator adds unitCents instead of the validated quantity * unitCents line amount, producing incorrect totals and invalid subsequent overflow checks.

repro.required: throw RangeError: the actual sum is 9007199254740992, exceeding Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER

action: Accumulate the validated extended line amount so sum checks use the actual running total. Added mixed/zero quantities, empty estimates, frozen records, safe boundary and product/sum overflow regressions.

cause: A strict less-than comparison rejects estimates equal to their budget.
action: Use <= for affordability. Added equal, zero, below-budget and above-budget regressions.
